description.value: The study compared decision making in behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia patients and healthy adults using the Balloon Analog Risk Task and investigated the relationship between BART performance and regional gray matter atrophy in bvFTD patients.

spans.text: The goal of this study was 2-fold. First, we were interested in comparing decision making in bvFTD patients and healthy adults using the BART and, second, we sought to investigate the relationship between BART performance and regional gray matter atrophy in bvFTD patients.

value: we hypothesized that bvFTD patients would not learn and would display impaired BART performance and impaired decision making, characterized as pumping below the average rate in healthy individuals.
We also predicted a positive association between this diminished learning and degree of atrophy in the lateral OFC

description.value: Images were reoriented, segmented into gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid, spatially normalized to the Montreal Neurological Institute template, modulated, and smoothed.

spans.text: All MR images were first reoriented according to the anterior commissure. Images were then segmented into gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid. Once segmented, the images were spatially normalized to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) template and modulated to transform all volume information into voxels. After the images were segmented, normalized, and modulated, they were smoothed with a 12 mm full width at half maximum Gaussian kernel.

One paradigm that can be used to study decision making is the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART)

description.value: A computer simulation of balloons that subjects inflate through pumping until the balloons explode or they decide to end the trial for a monetary reward.

spans.text: One paradigm that can be used to study decision making is the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART), a computer simulation of balloons that subjects inflate through pumping either until the balloons explode or patients decide to end the trial for a monetary reward that has been accumulated through repetitive pumping on a given trial.

instructions.value: Patients were instructed to pump up the balloon until either the balloon popped or they decided to stop pumping.

spans.text: Patients were instructed to pump up the balloon until 1 of 2 outcomes occurred: (i) either the balloon popped or (ii) the patient decided to stop pumping the balloon any larger.

stimuli.value: A mock balloon, a balloon pump, a reset button labeled “Collect $$$,” and a permanent total money earned display labeled “Total Earned.”

spans.text: An example of the BART computer display is shown in Figure 1, consisting of a mock balloon, a balloon pump labeled “Click Here to Pump Up Balloon,” a reset button labeled “Collect $$$,” and a permanent total money earned display labeled “Total Earned.”
Thirty trials were presented to the patients, who were instructed to use the mouse to pump up the balloon on each trial.

value: slope of the time course across 30 trials

spans.text: The output generated by the BART consists of 3 primary behavioral measures, each intended to serve as an alternate source of data to understand the risks and benefits associated with risk taking: (i) the number of pumps (a measure of the raw number of pumps and the average number of pumps); (ii) the number of explosions (a measure of how frequently the individual demonstrated excessive risk that led to a negative outcome); and (iii) the amount of money earned (an indication of how frequently the behavior of the individual resulted in not only a positive outcome, but how much risk was involved to maximize the monetary outcomes).
